cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: AWS is Amazon's public cloud: it rents servers, storage, databases and networking on demand, billed by usage, so you do not buy and size hardware up front.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: It runs in Regions, each with multiple isolated Availability Zones; spread workloads across AZs for high availability. IAM decides whether every API call is allowed. Security is shared: AWS secures the physical infrastructure, you secure IAM permissions, network rules, data and what runs on EC2.

questions.q: Is your app highly available just because it runs on AWS?
questions.a: No. AWS provides building blocks like multiple AZs, load balancers and Multi-AZ databases; you must use them.
A Region is a separate geographic area; an AZ is an isolated location within a Region.
Decides whether each AWS API call is allowed.
